Minecraft. A sandbox survival game released by Mojang in 2011 where players explore infinitely procedurally generated cube-based worlds. You gather resources and craft tools to build structures and survive against monsters. Its creative freedom and accessibility made it a cultural phenomenon, becoming the best-selling video game of all time with over three hundred million copies sold across all platforms. The game procedurally generates infinite blocky landscapes using a voxel-based engine, and you can place and destroy any block to reshape the world. It offers three core modes: Survival, where you gather resources and manage hunger and health; Creative, with unlimited blocks and flight; and Adventure, where you explore hand-crafted maps. Crafting requires combining raw materials in a three by three grid to create tools, weapons, and building materials—the foundation of progression. Nighttime spawns hostile mobs like Creepers, Skeletons, and Zombies, forcing you to fortify shelters or fight to survive. The Nether, an underworld dimension accessed via obsidian portals, and The End, a dimension containing the final boss called the Ender Dragon, extend exploration. The game was originally created solo by Markus "Notch" Persson and later expanded into a global community with yearly Minecraft Live events and massive multiplayer servers. It has also spawned Minecraft: Education Edition, used in schools to teach STEM, history, and creative problem-solving.
